topic: Fulcrum LNG selection, ExxonMobil gas appraisal, and pre-election freeze (2024-2026)
wiki_text: The proposed Guyana LNG / offshore gas-monetization project stems from the Guyanese government's drive to commercialize associated and non-associated gas from the ExxonMobil-operated Stabroek Block (beyond the onshore Wales Gas-to-Energy power project fed by the Gas-to-Energy pipeline). In 2024 the government selected US startup Fulcrum LNG — led by a former ExxonMobil executive — as the No.1-ranked bidder among 17 proposals to design, finance, build and operate offshore gas-gathering and LNG infrastructure. ExxonMobil affirmed support for developing Guyana's gas but, as of early 2026, had NOT committed to participating and was still appraising the resource (deeper geological zones and the south-east Stabroek area). Commentators questioned whether the little-known Fulcrum had the expertise and capital for a project potentially costing up to ~$30 billion. Vice President Bharrat Jagdeo said in June 2025 that no agreement with Fulcrum would be signed before the 1 September 2025 general elections; no signed agreement had been reported afterward. The project therefore remained pre-FID with no official name, no firmed capacity, and only an approximate Stabroek-vicinity location as of this sweep.
